findings.description: promote.py accepts slug from sys.argv[1] without path traversal validation. A malicious slug like '../../etc/passwd' constructs BACKLOG_DIR / '../../etc/passwd.json', allowing reads of arbitrary JSON files outside the backlog directory. run.py has explicit path traversal checks on UUID but promote.py has none on slug.

slugify() can return an empty string when the title is all special characters (e.g., '!!!', '$$$'). This produces a file named '.json' in the backlog directory, corrupts the board.md row (empty slug column), and creates an unmatchable slug for promote.py.

Pipe characters ('|') in the ticket title are not escaped or stripped before insertion into board.md table rows. A title like 'Fix | Urgent' corrupts the markdown table structure, breaking all subsequent board.md parsing by promote.py and run.py.

Spec says missing required args without --from-todo should produce argparse usage error and exit code 2. Code uses manual validation and sys.exit(1) instead, so exit code is always 1 for missing fields, violating the spec.

promote.py line 51 accesses data['title'], data['problem'], data['description'], data['scope'], data['created_at'] with direct dict key access. If a manually-created or corrupted backlog JSON is missing any of these keys, it raises an unhandled KeyError instead of a user-friendly error message.

promote.py update_board_row matches rows with line.startswith(f'| {slug} '). If two slugs share a prefix where one is the other plus a space (unlikely but possible, e.g., 'fix' vs 'fix '), the wrong row could be updated. More practically, if the board has been manually edited with different spacing, the match fails silently.

promote.py writes the intake file (line 68), then validates (line 70-77), then deletes backlog (line 79). If the process is killed between writing intake and deleting backlog, the system is in an inconsistent state: both files exist. The board still says 'backlog' but an intake file exists with a UUID that nothing tracks.

run.py update_board_status uses splitlines(keepends=True) and ''.join(), while promote.py update_board_row uses splitlines() and '
'.join() + '
'. The inconsistent line-ending handling means if board.md uses 
 (Windows), run.py preserves it but promote.py converts to 
, potentially causing mixed line endings after both tools touch the file.

responses.description: Added slug validation in promote.py after sys.argv[1] — rejects slugs containing '/', '\', null bytes, '.', '..', or any path with a directory component, matching the pattern already used for UUID validation in run.py.
Added empty-slug check in draft_ticket.py after slugify() — if the result is empty, prints a user-friendly error and exits with code 1 before any file operations.
In append_board_row(), title is now sanitized with title.replace('|', '\|') before interpolation into the board.md table row, preventing pipe characters from corrupting the table structure.
Replaced sys.exit(1) in the missing-fields branch with parser.error(), which prints the argparse usage header and exits with code 2 as required by the spec.

Added upfront required-key validation in promote.py before constructing the intake dict — checks all five required keys and emits a human-readable error naming the missing fields instead of raising KeyError.

Rewrote update_board_row() in promote.py to split on '|' and compare cols[1].strip() == slug (exact column match) instead of line.startswith(), eliminating false matches from prefix collisions or manual spacing changes.

Requires an OS-level process kill in the narrow window between intake_path.write_text() and backlog_path.unlink() — two consecutive lines with no blocking I/O between them. The next promote.py or run.py invocation will not be confused by the orphaned intake file. Fixing atomically (temp file + rename) adds non-trivial complexity for a low-severity, low-probability race; deferring until a cleanup/recovery pass is added to the pipeline.

Rewrote update_board_row() in promote.py to use splitlines(keepends=True) + ''.join() (same pattern as run.py), preserving original line endings (
 or 
) instead of converting all to 
.
